brief:
Workplace separation tests families across the world, but the particular pressures of Gaza's economy amplify the strain on relationships and household stability. The absence of breadwinners — whether by necessity or circumstance — leaves lasting marks on children and partners navigating restricted opportunities and limited resources, according to We Are Not Numbers. Fathers working away from home face an anguish compounded by Gaza's constraints: fewer job options, reduced ability to support dependents remotely, and the psychological weight of prolonged separation in a territory already marked by instability.

The emotional toll falls unevenly across households. Daughters and other family members adapt to an absent parent's presence, developing resilience born of necessity rather than choice. Economic pressures in Gaza make such separations not a temporary hardship but a defining feature of family life for many.
dek: Work-related separation is not uncommon. In Gaza, the ache of absence is more acute.
title: Gaza father's work separation deepens family strain
